pair.title: Connect your Android device
pair.subtitle: Homey connects over Wi-Fi using Android's Wireless debugging. No computer or cable needed.
pair.help_show: How do I pair my device?
pair.address_note: Both are shown under IP address & Port on the Wireless debugging screen.
pair.pairing_note: Tap Pair device with pairing code on the device and keep that dialog open. The pairing port is the number after the colon in the dialog. It is not the same as the port above.
pair.footer:
Menu names can differ a little between Android versions. Can't find it? Search for "build number" and "wireless debugging" in Settings.

Good to know: Android turns Wireless debugging off when the device restarts. Turn it back on afterwards; Homey reconnects by itself and no new code is needed.
pair.common_1: Make sure the device is on the same Wi-Fi network as Homey.
pair.common_2: Turn on Wireless debugging and confirm with Allow. Tick "Always allow on this network".
pair.common_3: Tap the words Wireless debugging (not the switch) to open its screen.
pair.common_4: Go back to the form and enter the IP address & Port shown on that screen.
pair.common_5: Tap Pair device with pairing code. Enter the 6-digit code and the port after the colon in the form.
pair.common_6: Keep that dialog open on the device and press Connect.
pair.oneplus_unlock_2: Tap Build number 7 times and enter your PIN. You see "You are now in Developer mode".
pair.oneplus_where: Go back to Settings › System settings (or Additional settings) › Developer options.
pair.oneplus_tip: Screen does not react to Homey? In Developer options, turn on Disable permission monitoring. These brands block remote button presses without it.
pair.samsung_unlock_1: Open Settings › About phone (or About tablet) › Software information.
pair.samsung_unlock_2: Tap Build number 7 times and enter your PIN.
pair.samsung_where: Go back to Settings and open Developer options at the very bottom.
pair.samsung_tip: If Wireless debugging is greyed out, turn off Auto Blocker under Settings › Security and privacy first.
pair.pixel_unlock_2: Tap Build number 7 times and enter your PIN.
pair.xiaomi_where: Go to Settings › Additional settings › Developer options.
pair.xiaomi_tip: Also turn on USB debugging (Security settings) in Developer options. Without it Xiaomi blocks turning the screen on and off. This needs a Mi account and sometimes a SIM card.
pair.lenovo_unlock_2: Tap Build number 7 times and enter your PIN.
pair.lenovo_tip: Tip for wall tablets: also turn on Stay awake in Developer options if the screen should stay on while charging.
pair.old_1: These devices have no Wireless debugging, so there is no pairing code. They use classic network ADB on port 5555 instead.
pair.old_2: Turn on Developer options (Settings › About › tap Build number or Serial number 7 times) and enable USB debugging (Fire tablet: ADB debugging).
pair.old_3: Some devices have an ADB over network switch in Developer options: turn it on. Otherwise connect the device to a computer once with a cable and run adb tcpip 5555.
pair.old_4: In the form, enter the IP address of the device and port 5555. Leave the pairing fields empty.
pair.old_5: Press Connect, then tick Always allow from this computer and tap Allow on the device.
pair.old_tip: Without an "ADB over network" switch, port 5555 closes again when the device restarts and the cable step has to be repeated.
